title: The Marrero bass-playing brothers and Zardis's schooling
summary: Simon, Eddie and Lawrence Marrero as fellow bassists who shared lessons, where they lived, and Zardis's school years and Catholic upbringing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: but I mean it would give me an idea, you know what I mean? Who were some of the other good bass players? Well he's starting, Bill Moran's son. Simon. You ever heard of Simon? Yeah I've heard of Simon. You got a record of him? No, I don't think he made any, yeah he made some records for Settles to him, but otherwise I never knew him.

Well that's another nice boy. And then he got another brother, played bass too, Eddie. Eddie Moran. Yeah we interviewed him. And Lawrence Moran, you got him too didn't you? Well that's all brothers. So we all came up just as brothers, because we used to go down there and Simon would take the bass, I'd take the bass, and you know what I mean, we'd get together with one another, the show one another. Where did they live in those days? They was living down at Spain Street on Spain between Vire and Oikwar. That's where they were living at that time because sometimes I would go to school and I'd leave my school and go around there because Maronese Street is not far from there, it's about two blocks from where they were staying. And I'd go to school over there. I mean I'd go there alone because, see I was just about finished up almost then because I was in I think it was seventh grade then. And I stayed there until, well I finished eighth grade over there. You mentioned something about a Catholic school, were you raised as a Catholic? No, that's a public school, that was a public school. You weren't raised as a Catholic. Yes I was raised as a Catholic. I'm still a Catholic. I'm still, yeah. You see, I keep there. Yeah, because I made first community right up here at St. Catherine.
